sites.evidence_type: N-terminal HA epitope; parallel surface-display screen
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface immunostaining PME 702.4 ± 98.9 (HA immunostaining, Tedman deep receptor scanning)
sites.rationale: Experimentally validated N-terminal HA epitope insertion (after signal-peptide cleavage where present); surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in Tedman et al. deep receptor scanning.

sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)
sources.claim: N-terminal HA epitope inserted per receptor; surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in a pooled GPCRome deep-receptor-scanning screen.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by anti-FLAG M2-FITC staining of non-permeabilized cells; no functional (cAMP or ligand-binding) assay was reported specifically for the N-terminal FLAG tag in isolation.
sites.rationale: GPR119 has no endogenous signal peptide in the canonical 335-aa sequence; residues 1–6 are extracellular and TM1 begins at residue 7. A prepend (insert_after_residue = 0) places the tag before M1 on the extracellular face, ≥6 residues from the TM1 boundary. No residue number is named in any ledger line, but the N-terminus is the only extracellular terminus of this 7-TM receptor, so the junction is unambiguous and topology-derived. Python confirmed residue_after = 'M' (seq[0]). Full-length human GPR119 (residues 1–335) engineered with an exogenous HA signal peptide followed by a FLAG tag (and bRIL) at the N-terminus; after HA-SP cleavage the FLAG is displayed on the extracellular face. Cell-surface expression confirmed by incubating non-permeabilized HEK293 cells with anti-FLAG M2-FITC antibody at 4 °C (live-cell staining).

sources.claim: The cell surface GPR119 expression level was detected by incubating 10 μl of cells with 10 μl of monoclonal anti-FLAG M2–fluorescein isothiocyanate antibody (Sigma-Aldrich) at 4 °C for 20 min in the dark.

literature_notes: L2 (PMC9671963) and L4/L3 (PMC10823026) also describe C-terminal FLAG/strep tags and L5 (PMC11625002) describes C-terminal LgBiT/eGFP; all C-terminal additions fall within the intracellular domain (residues 281–335 per topology landmarks) and are recorded in other_positions. L3 reports surface FLAG staining for the PMC10823026 construct, which also carries an N-terminal FLAG (same architecture as L1); L3 is therefore corroborating evidence for the same N-terminal site already grounded in L1, not a separate site. L5 describes a construct with N-terminal FLAG confirmed on the surface and C-terminal LgBiT/eGFP used for BRET/NanoBiT signalling assays; the signalling assay validates receptor function but is confounded by the presence of the large bRIL fusion and cannot be cleanly attributed to the FLAG tag alone, so validation_level remains surface_only. No ledger line supports any internal extracellular loop insertion for GPR119.

literature_other_positions.note: FLAG and strep tags fused after the C-terminal residue (G335); the C-terminus (residues 281–335) is intracellular per topology landmarks, so these tags face the cytoplasm and cannot serve as extracellular surface labels.
LgBiT and eGFP fused to the C-terminus after G335; same intracellular location as above, used for NanoBiT/BRET signalling assays rather than surface display.
